original_value: SummaryWireless sensor networks (WSNs) are widely used in large areas of applications; due to advancements in technology, very tiny sensors are readily available, and their usage reduces the cost. The mechanisms designed for wireless networks cannot be implied on networks with tiny nodes due to battery and computational constraints. Understanding the significance of security in WSNs and resource constraintness of tiny WSNs, we propose a node authentication mechanism for nodes in wireless sensor networks to avoid security attacks and establish secure communication between them. In the proposed mechanism, a base station (BS) generates a secret value and random value for each sensor node and stores at the node. The sensor node authenticates using secret value and random number. Random nonce ensures freshness, efficiency, and robustness. The proposed mechanism is lightweight cryptographic, hence requires very less computational, communication, and storage resources. Security analysis of the proposed mechanism could not detect any security attack on it, and the mechanism was found to incur less storage, communication, and computation overheads. Hence, the proposed mechanism is best suitable for wireless sensor networks with tiny nodes.

result.paraphrase: SummaryWireless sensor networks (WSNs) are widely applied across many domains; advances in technology have made very small sensors readily available, and their use lowers cost. Because tiny nodes face battery and computing limits, mechanisms designed for general wireless networks cannot be applied directly. Recognizing both the importance of security in WSNs and the resource constraints of small WSNs, we propose a node authentication scheme for wireless sensor network nodes to prevent security attacks and enable secure communication between them. In this scheme, a base station (BS) creates a secret value and a random value for each sensor node and stores them at the node. The sensor node then authenticates using the secret value and random number. A random nonce provides freshness, efficiency, and robustness. The proposed mechanism is lightweight cryptographic, so it needs very little computation, communication, and storage resources. Security analysis did not reveal any attacks against it, and it was found to impose lower storage, communication, and computation overheads. Therefore, the proposed mechanism is best suited for wireless sensor networks with tiny nodes.
